verdict.rationale: Zoom's public, machine-readable docs cover the whole agent loop. There is an OpenAPI spec, llms.txt and markdown pages. A synchronous POST /aiservices/scribe/transcribe returns the transcript directly, and batch mode documents job creation, status polling, per-file retrieval and signed completion webhooks, so a key-holding agent needs no human step after submission. Missing for 10: step-by-step detail on turning the API key into a JWT and calling with it (only briefly mentioned), and any hands-on or independent report of an agent completing the flow end to end.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent holding an API key can take a recording from submission to finished transcript (auth, job creation, result retrieval) from the public docs alone, with no human step in between

citations.quote: Batch mode documents POST /aiservices/scribe/jobs plus get-status, list-jobs, cancel-job, list-files, and get-file endpoints.
Fast mode provides synchronous transcription for individual audio files. The response returns immediately after the transcription completes.
Use a short-lived JWT for client-to-backend API calls.
six Scribe paths covering synchronous, live, batch-job, status, and per-file operations
